title: Pokemon Emerald Seaglass (v3.0)
sources: The ROM itself (Emerald Seaglass 3.0, pokeemerald-expansion based): region map section names (each place resolves to a section with maps) and trainer names, teams and levels, read on the PC with throwaway tools
pret/pokeemerald: Emerald's story order and fight places, which Seaglass keeps
pokemonemeraldseaglass.com, PokéHarbor (2024-08) and poke-hack-hub: features, retypes, evolution items
A fan 'Professor Oak Challenge' guide for Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs): legendary locations
Seaglass 3.0 official documentation by Nemo622 (PDF, mirrored at pokeporto.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Pokemon-Emerald-Seaglass-Documentation-v3.0.pdf): items, legendaries, minigames
Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide for Seaglass 3.0 (docs.google.com/document/d/1sqlBgI44MwvRo13Osqk5DmJ7oosxmg05CSC0ALs1ZAI): route-by-route walkthrough
PokéHarbor's Seaglass page (pokeharbor.com/?p=52602): the v2.0-v3.0 changelogs
The ROM's event scripts (Seaglass 3.0): the legendary encounters' species and levels (setvar/setwildbattle), read on the PC

milestones.name: Choose a starter (Route 101)
milestones.tips: Save Professor Birch from a Zigzagoon with a starter from his bag. All three are wild in the Safari Zone later (Mudkip south-west, Torchic north-west, Treecko south-east).
milestones.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

milestones.name: Rival: first battle (Route 103)
milestones.tips: May or Brendan (whichever you didn't pick; both are playable since 3.0) uses the starter strong against yours at Lv 5.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald story order (Seaglass keeps Emerald's)

milestones.name: Team Aqua in Petalburg Woods
milestones.tips: A grunt with a Lv 9 Wailmer bothers a Devon researcher. Grass or Electric moves.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald story order (Seaglass keeps Emerald's)

milestones.name: Gym 1: Roxanne
milestones.badge_note: Stone Badge: Cut (Seaglass needs the HM and the badge, not a move slot).
milestones.tips: Rock types (fossils first): Anorith, Lileep, Nosepass (Lv 12-15). Water, Grass, Fighting and Steel moves; Lileep is Grass/Rock (Ice, Fighting, Bug, Steel).
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald story order (Seaglass keeps Emerald's)

milestones.name: Team Aqua in Rusturf Tunnel
milestones.tips: A grunt with stolen Devon goods: Lv 11 Wailmer. Mr. Briney then sails you to Dewford.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald story order (Seaglass keeps Emerald's)

milestones.name: Rival: Rustboro City
milestones.tips: Your neighbour's second team, Lv 13-15.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald story order (Seaglass keeps Emerald's)

milestones.name: Gym 2: Brawly
milestones.tips: Fighting types: Makuhita, Meditite, Heracross (Lv 16-19). Psychic, Flying and Fairy moves; Heracross takes four times from Flying.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald story order (Seaglass keeps Emerald's)

milestones.name: Letter for Steven (Granite Cave)
milestones.tips: Mr. Briney sails you from Route 104 to Dewford. A hiker on the first floor gives HM05 Flash; Steven waits in the last room. A King's Rock lies on the shore above the cave's entrance.
milestones.source: Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs); Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF)

milestones.name: Team Aqua at the Oceanic Museum
milestones.tips: Two grunts at the museum (the ROM's at 14-15: Lombre and Carvanha). Electric and Grass moves.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald story order (Seaglass keeps Emerald's)

milestones.name: Rival: Route 110
milestones.tips: Three Pokémon now, the starter's second stage at Lv 20.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald story order (Seaglass keeps Emerald's)

milestones.name: Wally in Mauville
milestones.tips: Wally challenges you outside the gym with his Lv 16 Ralts.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald story order (Seaglass keeps Emerald's)

milestones.name: Gym 3: Wattson
milestones.tips: Electric types: Volbeat, Flaaffy, Magneton, Manectric (Lv 20-24). Ground moves above all; Volbeat is Bug (Fire, Flying, Rock).
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald story order (Seaglass keeps Emerald's)

milestones.name: The Winstrate family (Route 111)
milestones.tips: Four battles in a row in their house south of the desert: Victor (Pidgeotto, Zigzagoon, Lv 16), Victoria (Sunflora 17), Vivi (Marill, Tangela, Numel, Lv 15), Vicky (Meditite 18).
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald (Route111_WinstrateFamilysHouse)

milestones.name: Gabby & Ty (interview double battles)
milestones.tips: The TV crew double-battles you on Hoenn's routes as in Emerald; their team grows each time: Magnemite and Whismur at 17, up to Magnezone and Exploud at 39.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald (Gabby & Ty scripts)

milestones.name: Team Magma at Mt. Chimney
milestones.tips: Tabitha (Numel, Poochyena, Dunsparce, Houndour (Lv 18-22)) and Maxie (Mightyena, Gligar, Camerupt (Lv 24-25)) at the summit. Water and Ground moves. Two grunts (Dunsparce or Gligar, Lv 20) guard the way.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald story order (Seaglass keeps Emerald's)

milestones.name: Gym 4: Flannery
milestones.tips: Fire types: Slugma, Flareon, Camerupt, Torkoal (Lv 24-29). Water, Ground and Rock moves; Camerupt takes four times from Water.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald story order (Seaglass keeps Emerald's)

milestones.name: Gym 5: Norman
milestones.tips: Normal types: Spinda, Vigoroth, Politoed, Slaking (Lv 27-31). Fighting moves; Politoed is Water (Grass, Electric). Slaking loafs every other turn: protect or switch on its active turns.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald story order (Seaglass keeps Emerald's)

milestones.name: Team Aqua at the Weather Institute
milestones.tips: Grunts at Lv 26-28 (Murkrow, Masquerain, Electabuzz, Persian and Carvanha among them), then Shelly: Ludicolo, Mightyena (Lv 28). Flying or Poison moves for Ludicolo, Fighting or Fairy for Mightyena. You get a Castform afterwards.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs); pret/pokeemerald story order

milestones.name: Rival: Route 119
milestones.tips: Lv 29-31 team; they give you HM02 Fly afterwards.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald story order (Seaglass keeps Emerald's)

milestones.name: Gym 6: Winona
milestones.tips: Flying types: Fearow, Tropius, Pelipper, Skarmory, Altaria (Lv 29-33). Electric, Ice and Rock moves; Skarmory is Steel/Flying (Fire, Electric).
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald story order (Seaglass keeps Emerald's)

milestones.name: Rival: Lilycove City
milestones.tips: Their last team: the final starter stage at Lv 36.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald story order (Seaglass keeps Emerald's)

milestones.name: Team Aqua at Mt. Pyre
milestones.tips: Aqua grunts on the way up: Arbok, Tentacruel (Lv 32), Mightyena and Carvanha, Wailmer and Cradily (Lv 30). Team Aqua leaves with the orb and you are given the Magma Emblem. Unown grow outside, Ditto at the foggy summit.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table (ids 22-24, 568); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

milestones.name: Team Magma Hideout (Jagged Pass)
milestones.tips: The Magma Emblem opens the hideout on Jagged Pass; a grunt (Gligar, Shiftry, Lv 22) guards the door. Inside, Tabitha (Numel, Dodrio, Murkrow, Camerupt (Lv 26-33)) and Maxie (Gliscor, Crobat, Ursaring, Camerupt (Lv 37-39)) wake Groudon. Water moves.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs); pret/pokeemerald (JaggedPass scripts)

milestones.name: Team Aqua Hideout
milestones.tips: Surf from Lilycove's north-east to the hideout; a Dubious Disc lies in the entrance room and the Master Ball in a side room (take the right warp pads). Matt: Mightyena, Golbat (Lv 34). Electric moves.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs); Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF)

milestones.name: Gym 7: Tate & Liza
milestones.tips: A double battle: Claydol, Mismagius, Lunatone, Solrock (Lv 41-42). Dark, Ghost, Water and Grass moves; Lunatone and Solrock fear Water and Grass.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald story order (Seaglass keeps Emerald's)

milestones.name: Team Magma at the Space Center
milestones.tips: Grunts (Lv 30-32) fill the Space Center. Seaglass dropped Emerald's multi battle beside Steven: Maxie fights you in a double battle with six Pokémon: Gliscor, Crobat, Shiftry, Ursaluna, Dodrio, Camerupt (Lv 42-44). Water and Ice moves.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; PokéHarbor: Seaglass changelog v2.0-3.0 (v2.0 fixes)

milestones.name: Seafloor Cavern: Archie
milestones.tips: Dive on Route 128. Grunts at Lv 35-36 and Shelly (Sharpedo, Whiscash, Lv 37) on the way, then Archie: Wailord, Breloom, Crobat, Sharpedo (Lv 41-43). Electric moves for Wailord, Sharpedo and Crobat; Flying or Psychic for Breloom.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald story order (Seaglass keeps Emerald's)

milestones.name: Rayquaza at Sky Pillar
milestones.tips: With both box legends awake over Sootopolis, climb Sky Pillar to wake Rayquaza and end the storm.
milestones.source: pret/pokeemerald story order (Seaglass keeps Emerald's)

milestones.name: Rayquaza (Sky Pillar)
milestones.tips: Once it has calmed Sootopolis, Wallace gives you a second Master Ball; go back to the top of Sky Pillar with the Mach Bike. Lv 70.
milestones.source: Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs); ROM 3.0 event scripts

milestones.name: Gym 8: Juan
milestones.badge_note: Rain Badge: Waterfall (the HM itself is the Scuba Safari's first prize). Juan gives TM Ice Beam instead of Water Pulse.
milestones.tips: Water types: Starmie, Whiscash, Sealeo, Octillery, Kingdra (Lv 41-46). Electric and Grass moves; Kingdra is Water/Dragon (Dragon, Fairy).
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; PokéHarbor: Seaglass changelog v2.0-3.0; Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF)

milestones.name: Wally (Victory Road)
milestones.tips: Altaria, Delcatty, Roserade, Magnezone, Gardevoir (Lv 41-45). Fire for Roserade, Ice for Altaria, Steel or Poison for Gardevoir.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald story order (Seaglass keeps Emerald's)

milestones.name: Elite Four: Sidney
milestones.tips: Mightyena, Honchkrow, Cacturne, Crawdaunt, Absol (Lv 46-49). Fighting, Bug and Fairy moves.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald story order (Seaglass keeps Emerald's)

milestones.name: Elite Four: Phoebe
milestones.tips: Dusclops, Froslass, Mismagius, Banette, Dusknoir (Lv 48-51). Dark and Ghost moves.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald story order (Seaglass keeps Emerald's)

milestones.name: Elite Four: Glacia
milestones.tips: Dewgong, Glalie, Glaceon, Cloyster, Walrein (Lv 50-53). Fire, Fighting, Rock and Steel moves.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald story order (Seaglass keeps Emerald's)

milestones.name: Elite Four: Drake
milestones.tips: Kingdra, Altaria, Steelix, Flygon, Salamence (Lv 52-55). Ice, Dragon and Fairy moves; Steelix wants Fire or Ground.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald story order (Seaglass keeps Emerald's)

milestones.name: Champion Wallace
milestones.tips: Wailord, Tentacruel, Ludicolo, Whiscash, Gyarados, Milotic (Lv 55-58). Electric and Grass moves; Ludicolo and Whiscash need others (Flying/Poison, Grass).
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald story order (Seaglass keeps Emerald's)

milestones.name: Post-game: Wally's rematches
milestones.tips: Wally returns stronger (the ROM has his team at 48, 51, 54 and 57).
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table

milestones.name: Post-game: Steven
milestones.tips: Steven in the deep part of Meteor Falls: Skarmory, Claydol, Aggron, Cradily, Armaldo, Metagross (Lv 75-78).
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald story order (Seaglass keeps Emerald's)

milestones.name: Post-game: Battle Frontier
milestones.tips: A fully working Battle Frontier (Battle Tent and Factory restored in 2.0). An NPC running laps at its entrance opens the EV/IV editor.
milestones.source: PokéHarbor: Seaglass changelog v2.0-3.0

milestones.name: Rematch: Roxanne
milestones.tips: The ROM keeps four stronger teams for Roxanne (aces at Lv 37, 42, 47 and 52), Emerald's Match Call rematches.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald (leader rematches)

milestones.name: Rematch: Brawly
milestones.tips: The ROM keeps four stronger teams for Brawly (aces at Lv 37, 42, 48 and 52), Emerald's Match Call rematches.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald (leader rematches)

milestones.name: Rematch: Wattson
milestones.tips: The ROM keeps four stronger teams for Wattson (aces at Lv 40, 45, 50 and 55), Emerald's Match Call rematches.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald (leader rematches)

milestones.name: Rematch: Flannery
milestones.tips: The ROM keeps four stronger teams for Flannery (aces at Lv 40, 45, 50 and 55), Emerald's Match Call rematches.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald (leader rematches)

milestones.name: Rematch: Norman
milestones.tips: The ROM keeps four stronger teams for Norman (aces at Lv 45, 50, 55 and 60), Emerald's Match Call rematches.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald (leader rematches)

milestones.name: Rematch: Winona
milestones.tips: The ROM keeps four stronger teams for Winona (aces at Lv 45, 50, 55 and 60), Emerald's Match Call rematches.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald (leader rematches)

milestones.name: Rematch: Tate & Liza
milestones.tips: The ROM keeps four stronger teams for Tate & Liza (aces at Lv 50, 55, 60 and 65), Emerald's Match Call rematches.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald (leader rematches)

milestones.name: Rematch: Juan
milestones.tips: The ROM keeps four stronger teams for Juan (aces at Lv 51, 56, 61 and 66), Emerald's Match Call rematches.
milestones.source: ROM Seaglass 3.0 trainer table; pret/pokeemerald (leader rematches)

milestones.name: Salon Maiden Anabel (Battle Tower)
milestones.tips: The Battle Tower's Frontier Brain; Seaglass 2.0 made every facility work. Pokémon are set to Lv 50 (or Open Level); a silver symbol at the first meeting, gold at the second.
milestones.source: PokéHarbor: Seaglass changelog v2.0-3.0; pret/pokeemerald (src/frontier_util.c)

milestones.name: Dome Ace Tucker (Battle Dome)
milestones.tips: The Battle Dome's Frontier Brain; Seaglass 2.0 made every facility work. Pokémon are set to Lv 50 (or Open Level); a silver symbol at the first meeting, gold at the second.
milestones.source: PokéHarbor: Seaglass changelog v2.0-3.0; pret/pokeemerald (src/frontier_util.c)

milestones.name: Palace Maven Spenser (Battle Palace)
milestones.tips: The Battle Palace's Frontier Brain; Seaglass 2.0 made every facility work. Pokémon are set to Lv 50 (or Open Level); a silver symbol at the first meeting, gold at the second.
milestones.source: PokéHarbor: Seaglass changelog v2.0-3.0; pret/pokeemerald (src/frontier_util.c)

milestones.name: Arena Tycoon Greta (Battle Arena)
milestones.tips: The Battle Arena's Frontier Brain; Seaglass 2.0 made every facility work. Pokémon are set to Lv 50 (or Open Level); a silver symbol at the first meeting, gold at the second.
milestones.source: PokéHarbor: Seaglass changelog v2.0-3.0; pret/pokeemerald (src/frontier_util.c)

milestones.name: Factory Head Noland (Battle Factory)
milestones.tips: The Battle Factory's Frontier Brain; Seaglass 2.0 made every facility work. Pokémon are set to Lv 50 (or Open Level); a silver symbol at the first meeting, gold at the second.
milestones.source: PokéHarbor: Seaglass changelog v2.0-3.0; pret/pokeemerald (src/frontier_util.c)

milestones.name: Pike Queen Lucy (Battle Pike)
milestones.tips: The Battle Pike's Frontier Brain; Seaglass 2.0 made every facility work. Pokémon are set to Lv 50 (or Open Level); a silver symbol at the first meeting, gold at the second.
milestones.source: PokéHarbor: Seaglass changelog v2.0-3.0; pret/pokeemerald (src/frontier_util.c)

milestones.name: Pyramid King Brandon (Battle Pyramid)
milestones.tips: The Battle Pyramid's Frontier Brain; Seaglass 2.0 made every facility work. Pokémon are set to Lv 50 (or Open Level); a silver symbol at the first meeting, gold at the second.
milestones.source: PokéHarbor: Seaglass changelog v2.0-3.0; pret/pokeemerald (src/frontier_util.c)

milestones.name: Mewtwo (Granite Cave)
milestones.tips: After the sailor's first three quests, talk to him in Steven's room at the end of Granite Cave: Mewtwo, Lv 80. A good use of a Master Ball.
milestones.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs); ROM 3.0 event scripts

milestones.name: Latios or Latias (Southern Island)
milestones.tips: After the 7th badge the eyepatch sailor in Mossdeep gives the S.S. Ticket and the Eon Ticket. One Lati, at random, at Lv 50; run and re-enter for the other one. The other comes after the League (also roaming).
milestones.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs); ROM 3.0 event scripts

milestones.name: Mew (Faraway Island)
milestones.tips: The sailor gives the Old Sea Map once you have Rhydon's Pokédex entry. Corner Mew in the grass; Lv 30.
milestones.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs); ROM 3.0 event scripts

milestones.name: Jirachi (Mossdeep's White Rock)
milestones.tips: Talk to the woman beside Mossdeep's White Rock, then check the rock with a Wishing Star in the bag. Lv 10.
milestones.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); ROM 3.0 event scripts

milestones.name: Deoxys (Birth Island)
milestones.tips: The sailor gives the Aurora Ticket once you have Rayquaza's Pokédex entry. Solve the triangle puzzle; Deoxys is Lv 70 and knows Recover.
milestones.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs); ROM 3.0 event scripts

milestones.name: Lugia and Ho-Oh (Navel Rock)
milestones.tips: Show the eyepatch sailor in Mossdeep Octillery's Pokédex entry for the Mystic Ticket; sail from Lilycove. Lugia (bottom floor) and Ho-Oh (top), both Lv 50, both catchable before the Champion.
milestones.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); ROM 3.0 event scripts; Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

milestones.name: Raikou, Entei or Suicune (Shoal Cave)
milestones.tips: After the sailor's first three quests he waits in Shoal Cave's ice room (lowest floor; reach it at low tide, clock 3-8 AM or PM) and summons one at random at Lv 50. The other two come after beating the Elite Four again.
milestones.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); ROM 3.0 event scripts; Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

milestones.name: Articuno, Zapdos or Moltres (Mt. Pyre)
milestones.tips: After the sailor's first three quests he summons one at random at Mt. Pyre's summit, Lv 50. Beat the Elite Four again for the next.
milestones.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); ROM 3.0 event scripts

milestones.name: Regirock, Regice, Registeel
milestones.tips: As in Emerald: dive on Route 134 to the Sealed Chamber, use Dig on the back wall, then read the inner wall with Wailord first and Relicanth last. Regirock (Desert Ruins, Route 111), Regice (Island Cave, Route 105), Registeel (Ancient Tomb, Route 120), each Lv 40.
milestones.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs); ROM 3.0 event scripts

milestones.name: Celebi (Route 119)
milestones.tips: After the sailor's first three quests: take the Acro Bike up behind the Weather Institute to the shrine north of it and talk to the sailor there. Lv 40.
milestones.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs); ROM 3.0 event scripts

milestones.name: Kyogre and Groudon (post-game)
milestones.tips: After the League, the scientist upstairs in the Weather Institute names a route with heavy rain (Kyogre, Marine Cave, Dive) or drought (Groudon, Terra Cave); both Lv 70. Their mist blocks sleep: paralyse instead.
milestones.source: Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs); Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); ROM 3.0 event scripts

steps.title: Set the difficulty in your room
steps.text: The book in your room turns Hard Mode (set style, no items in trainer battles) and the soft level cap (less EXP over the cap) on or off. The GameCube there takes cheat codes.
steps.source: pokemonemeraldseaglass.com; PokéHarbor

steps.title: Get a Linking Cord
steps.text: Lanette's house on Route 114 gives a Linking Cord for trade evolutions; more are prizes at the Mossdeep pinball.
steps.source: pokemonemeraldseaglass.com; PokéHarbor

steps.title: Rustboro wishing well
steps.text: Wishing Stars bought in the Rustboro wishing well give random Lv 1 Pokémon.
steps.source: pokemonemeraldseaglass.com; PokéHarbor

steps.title: Evolution stones in Lavaridge
steps.text: The Lavaridge herb shop sells the Leaf, Ice, Shiny and Dawn Stones.
steps.source: pokemonemeraldseaglass.com; PokéHarbor

steps.title: Z-Ring from Devon
steps.text: Devon gives a Z-Ring; Z-Crystals are sold in a shop.
steps.source: pokemonemeraldseaglass.com; PokéHarbor

steps.title: DexNav from Mom
steps.text: After Birch gives the Pokédex, your mother installs the DexNav as you leave Littleroot. Every ~200 steps it finds a nearby Pokémon, half the time a 'hidden' one; chaining raises shiny odds, IVs and egg-move chances.
steps.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF)

steps.title: Exp. Share from Scott
steps.text: Just after Wally's catching lesson, Scott stops you outside Petalburg with the Exp. Share: the whole party gains EXP, held back by the soft level cap.
steps.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

steps.title: Petalburg merchant stand
steps.text: The Happy Trainer stand in Petalburg sells EXP Candies, Ability Capsules, stat feathers, Choice items and vitamins; more stock unlocks with each badge. Pedro there adds Eviolite and Flame Orb after Gym 6, Loaded Dice and Toxic Orb after Gym 7.
steps.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); PokéHarbor: Seaglass changelog v2.0-3.0

steps.title: Nature mints on Route 104
steps.text: The Pretty Petal flower shop on Route 104 sells nature mints (and the Wailmer Pail for berries).
steps.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

steps.title: HM01 Cut in Rustboro
steps.text: The house next to Rustboro's Pokémon Center gives HM01 Cut; with the Stone Badge any Pokémon that can learn it cuts trees, no move slot needed.
steps.source: Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs); Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF)

steps.title: Littleroot's new grass
steps.text: After the Stone Badge, cut into the grass in Littleroot Town: Eevee, Mareep, Natu, Drowzee and the Applin line's Applin.
steps.source: Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs); Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF)

steps.title: Timer Balls
steps.text: A man on the Rustboro side of Rusturf Tunnel gives you a ball, and Rustboro's Mart then sells Timer Balls.
steps.source: Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

steps.title: Old Rod in Dewford
steps.text: A fisherman wandering Dewford gives the Old Rod. Horsea fished on Route 106 can hold a Dragon Scale.
steps.source: Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

steps.title: Stones at Slateport's market
steps.text: A stall in the market sells Water, Thunder, Fire, Sun and Moon Stones (no Leaf Stone yet). The Fan Club gives a Soothe Bell for a friendly lead.
steps.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

steps.title: Fly to Pacifidlog early
steps.text: After the museum fight, an NPC by Slateport's Pokémon Center takes you to Pacifidlog: grass with Scyther and Heracross, the apple seller and the Scuba Safari.
steps.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

steps.title: Scuba Safari
steps.text: The sailor on Pacifidlog's east platform runs it: 200 tiles and 5 encounters underwater, no Dive needed. Score = rarity + 3x level + IVs + HP left. The first high score gives HM07 Waterfall; also a cheap training spot (Lapras, Relicanth).
steps.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

steps.title: Route 110 without Cycling Road
steps.text: Cycling Road is gone in Seaglass. The Trick House is still here; the rival gives the Itemfinder after the fight.
steps.source: Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs); PokéHarbor: Seaglass changelog v2.0-3.0

steps.title: Bike, Rock Smash and pinball
steps.text: Mauville gives a free bike and HM06 Rock Smash. Its Game Corner's pinball wins Pinball Points for apricorn balls and Alolan-form eggs.
steps.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

steps.title: Good Rod on Route 118
steps.text: The Good Rod fisherman now stands on the near bank of Route 118, so you can get it before Surf.
steps.source: Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

steps.title: Contests in Verdanturf
steps.text: The Contest Hall moved to Verdanturf (an NPC there resets Sheen); the Battle Tent moved to Lilycove. A Metal Coat lies in Rusturf Tunnel's Verdanturf end.
steps.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

steps.title: Pokémon Box Link
steps.text: After Wattson, a scientist in Slateport's Pokémon Center gives the Box Link: the PC from anywhere. Clear Rusturf Tunnel's rocks for HM04 Strength.
steps.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

steps.title: North of Mauville
steps.text: The cable car stays shut until the Meteor Falls scene: walk Fiery Path, Route 113, Fallarbor and Route 114 first. Route 115's grass, south of Meteor Falls, is reachable too.
steps.source: Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

steps.title: HM03 Surf
steps.text: Norman's win opens Surf: Squirtle in Petalburg's water, Staryu on Route 107, a Metal Coat at the Abandoned Ship and Wattson's key to New Mauville.
steps.source: Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

steps.title: Devon Scope and the Fortree shrines
steps.text: Steven gives the Devon Scope on Route 120's bridge. In Fortree, check every shrine from east to west; the last one (left of the Pokémon Center) holds a second Shiny Charm.
steps.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

steps.title: Magma Emblem
steps.text: At Mt. Pyre's summit you receive the Magma Emblem; take it back to Jagged Pass to open the Magma Hideout. Then Team Aqua steals the submarine in Slateport.
steps.source: Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

steps.title: Mossdeep gifts
steps.text: The pinball hall gives a Lucky Egg; an NPC on the left side of town gives a King's Rock. Mossdeep pinball points trade for random rare items (Linking Cords among them).
steps.source: Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs); Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF)

steps.title: Sootopolis evolution stand
steps.text: With Dive from Steven, go straight to Sootopolis: the stand north of the Pokémon Center sells every evolution item (Protector, Reaper Cloth...). The story then blocks it until the next badge.
steps.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

steps.title: The eyepatch sailor
steps.text: After the 7th badge, a sailor with an eyepatch by Mossdeep's telescope gives the S.S. Ticket and Eon Ticket, then quests for the other legends. Stock Ultra and Timer Balls and a sleep or False Swipe user.
steps.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

steps.title: After the League
steps.text: Beating the Elite Four resets the random Lati, beast and bird encounters; beat them again to reach the rest of each trio.
steps.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

secrets.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF)

secrets.text: Aurora Ticket from the eyepatch sailor (needs Rayquaza's Pokédex entry): Deoxys, Lv 70, on Birth Island.

secrets.text: Talk to the woman by Mossdeep's White Rock, then check the rock with a Wishing Star in the bag: Jirachi.
secrets.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF)

secrets.text: The Safari Zone is buggy: save first. Mudkip lives in the south-west, Larvitar and Torchic in the north-west (Mach Bike).

secrets.source: pokemonemeraldseaglass.com; PokéHarbor

secrets.text: Pinball tables in Mauville and Mossdeep pay out prizes, Linking Cords among them.
secrets.source: pokemonemeraldseaglass.com; PokéHarbor

secrets.text: Magnezone: level Magneton in New Mauville, or use a Thunder Stone.

secrets.text: A Shiny Charm waits in your bedroom PC from the start (shiny odds 1/4096 without it).

secrets.text: After Steven gets the letter, Devon gives the Z-Power Ring; Z-Crystals are sold on the floor below. Entirely optional.
secrets.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

secrets.text: Wishing Stars: one on the ground by the Rustboro well, more from a girl in Rustboro and a hiker in Granite Cave, and sold on Mt. Chimney once the teams are gone.

secrets.text: A hiker on Granite Cave's first floor gives HM05 Flash.
secrets.source: Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

secrets.text: A King's Rock lies on Route 106 just above Granite Cave's entrance; used like a stone it evolves Slowpoke or Poliwhirl.
secrets.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

secrets.text: The Pokémon Fan Club gives a Soothe Bell when your lead is friendly enough.

secrets.text: Pokémon Box Link from the scientist in the Pokémon Center, after Wattson.
secrets.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF)

secrets.text: A Metal Coat lies at Rusturf Tunnel's Verdanturf end (Onix or Scyther).
secrets.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

secrets.text: A second Metal Coat sits at the Abandoned Ship's entrance (needs Surf).

secrets.text: A Dragon Scale lies on Route 118 (Seadra to Kingdra).

secrets.text: The Electirizer lies in New Mauville in place of Emerald's Ultra Ball.

secrets.text: A Razor Fang lies in the west side of Route 119's tall grass (Gligar).
secrets.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

secrets.text: Black Augurite lies in the grass up and right after Route 119's bridge (Scyther to Kleavor).
secrets.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

secrets.text: The Weather Institute holds an Upgrade (Porygon) and, upstairs, a Linking Cord.
secrets.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

secrets.source: Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

secrets.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

secrets.text: Lanette's house on Route 114 holds a Linking Cord.

secrets.text: An NPC on Mossdeep's west side gives a second King's Rock.

notes.title: Emerald Seaglass 3.0
notes.text: Emerald redrawn in a Game Boy Color style with Emerald's story. All Gen I-III species, their later evolutions and a few newer ones; Fairy type and the split. 3.0 adds Brendan and May as playable and new leader sprites.

notes.title: Retyped Pokémon
notes.text: Noctowl Ghost/Flying, Sceptile Grass/Dragon, Octillery Water/Fire, Meganium Grass/Fairy, Typhlosion Fire/Ground, Feraligatr Water/Dark, Blastoise Water/Steel, Hypno Psychic/Dark, Aggron Steel/Dragon, Huntail Water/Dragon, Gorebyss Water/Fairy, Ninjask Bug/Dark.

notes.title: Features
notes.text: Followers (can be turned off), DexNav, Box Link (the PC anywhere), HMs without move slots, party Exp. Share, Z-Moves, a shiny charm and a type-effectiveness display.

notes.title: More retypes and abilities
notes.text: Ekans and Arbok are Poison/Dark. Hypno's new ability Nasty Surprise confuses poisoned foes; the Meganium line's hidden ability is Triage; Ninjask gets Sharpness; Ho-Oh has Soul Heart, Lugia Water Power, Tyranitar's hidden ability is Earth Eater.
notes.source: PokéHarbor: Seaglass changelog v2.0-3.0; ROM Seaglass 3.0 species table

notes.title: Newer Pokémon
notes.text: Cross-generation evolutions up to Gen 9 (Annihilape, Farigiraf, Dudunsparce, Kleavor, Ursaluna, Wyrdeer, Roserade, Mamoswine...), Spiky-eared Pichu, the Applin line (Littleroot) and the Tinkatink line (Route 115 Egg).
notes.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); PokéHarbor: Seaglass changelog v2.0-3.0

notes.title: Alolan forms
notes.text: Alolan forms come from Mauville's pinball eggs. The ROM has Alolan Rattata, Raichu, Sandshrew, Vulpix, Diglett, Meowth, Geodude, Grimer, Exeggutor and Marowak; hatched evolved forms count as single-stage.
notes.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs); ROM Seaglass 3.0 species table

notes.title: The book on your desk
notes.text: Toggles Hard Mode (Set style, no Bag in trainer battles), the soft level cap (EXP halves past the next leader's top level, then drops more), K.O. animations and battle backgrounds. R toggles auto-run.
notes.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); PokéHarbor: Seaglass changelog v2.0-3.0

notes.title: GameCube codes
notes.text: The GameCube in your room takes codes from the documentation: Rare Candies, Master Balls, Wishing Stars, Nuggets, every starter trio, Applin and Tinkatink, DexNav reveal, and MONO codes that give a random first-stage Pokémon of one type.

notes.title: Following Pokémon
notes.text: Every Pokémon can follow you. The party menu's FOLLOWER option sets a preferred follower or returns it to its ball.

notes.title: HMs without move slots
notes.text: With the HM in the bag and the right badge, any party Pokémon able to learn it uses the field move. Disobedience is gone too.
notes.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); PokéHarbor: Seaglass changelog v2.0-3.0

notes.title: The Mossdeep sailor's legends
notes.text: The eyepatch sailor (after Gym 7) unlocks the Eon Ticket, Old Sea Map (Rhydon seen), Mystic Ticket (Octillery seen) and Aurora Ticket (Rayquaza seen); then Celebi, Mewtwo, a beast and a bird.

notes.title: One of each trio per League
notes.text: The beasts (Shoal Cave) and birds (Mt. Pyre) are summoned one at random at Lv 50; each Elite Four win resets them. Latias/Latios also roam after the League.

notes.title: Emerald's own legends
notes.text: Kyogre, Groudon, Rayquaza (Lv 70) and the Regis (Lv 40) are found the way Emerald does it.
notes.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); ROM Seaglass 3.0 event scripts

notes.title: Scuba Safari scoring
notes.text: Rarity + level x3 + the six IVs + HP left. After the first prize (HM07 Waterfall) rewards are random treasures and items; a new high score is meant to add 5 Heart Scales and a good TM (the Oak guide never got these).
notes.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); Mewlax's Professor Oak Challenge guide, Seaglass 3.0 (Google Docs)

notes.title: Pinball
notes.text: Meowth, Gengar, Seel and Diglett tables in Mauville and Mossdeep; a win is 1 Pinball Point. Mossdeep sells points for money and pays random rare items. Start quits a stuck game.
notes.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); PokéHarbor: Seaglass changelog v2.0-3.0

notes.title: Rustboro Wishing Well
notes.text: A Wishing Star thrown in the well on Rustboro's east side gives a random Lv 1 Pokémon.
notes.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); PokéHarbor: Seaglass changelog v2.0-3.0

notes.title: Battle changes
notes.text: Absorb 30 and Mega Drain 50 power; Bubble 30 and always lowers Speed; Eviolite blocks evolution like an Everstone; every Pokémon has at least two perfect IVs (A on the summary shows IVs/EVs).
notes.source: PokéHarbor: Seaglass changelog v2.0-3.0; Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF)

notes.title: 3.0 balance
notes.text: Light Ball works for Pichu, Raichu and Spiky-eared Pichu (wild Pichu may hold one); Spinda learns Fiery Dance and Superpower; Aggron Dragon Dance; Farfetch'd Victory Dance; Drowzee and Hypno get Dark moves.

notes.title: Known issues
notes.text: Save before DexNav chaining (it can freeze, mostly in caves). Safari Zone battles act as normal battles and its UI is buggy; an NPC warns you at the gate.
notes.source: Seaglass 3.0 documentation (Nemo622, PDF); PokéHarbor: Seaglass changelog v2.0-3.0
